_comment: PROPOSAL, not implemented. P2P Stage 1, first slice. The project key: who holds it,
how a member gets it, how the owner rotates it, what happens when a member leaves.
Started here because it is the one place a whole project can be lost. Every other
failure in the design loses a snapshot or a connection; losing the key loses
everything ever encrypted under it.
Authority: ledger decisions of 2026-09-04 (d6758d5..3647b8a). Terms from there:
эх үүсвэр                        = the working file (DWG/RVT/MAX). Never travels.
эх үүсвэрээс гаралтай мэдээлэл   = derived output (sheet package, meta, quantities).
This is what travels, encrypted under the project key.
Server (erk-s.mn) holds licence, membership, the live layer and statistics. It never
sees output content. The escrow ring below is membership data, not content: it holds
WRAPPED keys the server cannot open.
Addressing is by code, never by IP. A bot's code is the hash of its own public key,
so it certifies itself: whoever can sign with the key IS that code. One key pair per
bot, kept in Windows Credential Manager under the seated Windows user - the same
boundary the SSO identity record uses (one Windows user = one device).
identities._botCode: = base32(sha256(botPublicKey))[0..16]. Server-registered too (SRV bot identity), but verifiable without the server.
identities._twoKeys: Ed25519 signs (snapshots, invitations). X25519 wraps (the project key). Never the same key for both.
_projectCode: The project's stable name across every device and network. Derived from the founder's
signing key + a random salt at creation, so two founders cannot collide and a code
cannot be guessed from a name. NOT the local Guid.NewGuid in project.erksproject
(RFC-003 §35: that one is user-authored and proves nothing) and NOT the server's
srv_prj id (that one needs the server). This code works offline and on a LAN.

_comment: One symmetric key per project per key version. Encrypts every snapshot payload.
It exists in the clear ONLY inside a running Studio that has unwrapped it - never in
a file, never on the server, never in a snapshot.
_keyVersion: Monotonic per project. Rotated by the owner (below). Every snapshot names the version
it was sealed under, and a device keeps the history of versions it was given, so old
snapshots stay readable after a rotation. Nothing is re-encrypted on rotation.

_comment: WHERE THE KEY LIVES: wrapped once per member, to that member's X25519 key. The ring
is the project's membership list with a wrapped key beside each entry.
The ring is stored in the LIVE LAYER on the server (membership is server-owned, and
joining/leaving is exactly when the ring changes) AND carried inside every snapshot
manifest, so a device that is offline for a month still has the ring as of its last
snapshot. Two copies, one meaning: the server's is canon, the snapshot's is the
offline fallback.
escrowRing._ringSequence: Server-issued counter (the live layer's CAS). An edit based on a stale sequence is refused; the owner pulls and redoes it. Offline, the ring is read-only.

members.wrappedKey: <AES key sealed to this bot's X25519 key, HPKE, base64>

escrowRing.ringSignature: <Ed25519 over (projectCode, keyVersion, ringSequence, members[]) by the owner>
_ringSignature: The owner signs the ring. A member accepts a ring only if it is signed by the owner
key it already trusts for this project (learned from the invitation). So the server
cannot add a member, and a member cannot add a member - only the owner's key can,
wherever the ring happens to be stored. [[self-declared-fields-prove-nothing]]

_comment: How a member gets in. The owner signs an invitation naming the invitee's bot code;
the invitee presents it; the owner (or the server's live layer, on the owner's behalf
using the owner's pre-signed ring update) adds the wrapped key. The invitee's device
key never leaves the invitee's machine - only its PUBLIC half travels.
invitation.signature: <Ed25519 by the owner over all fields above>
invitation._deliveredAs: A QR code or a short code typed in. Contains the fields, not the project key - the key arrives only as a wrapped entry in the ring, sealed to the invitee's own key.
invitation._acceptance: Two-sided, same rule as RFC-003 §3: the owner invites, the person accepts on their own device. Nobody accepts on someone's behalf.

_comment: A member leaves (or is removed). Their ring entry is deleted AND the owner rotates:
new keyVersion, new AES key, re-wrapped for every remaining member, new ring sequence.
Why rotate and not just delete the entry: the departed device still holds the old
key in memory/history and can read any snapshot sealed under it. Deleting the entry
stops them getting FUTURE keys; rotation stops them reading FUTURE snapshots. Both
are needed; neither is enough alone.
_whatTheyKeep: Everything they already received, readable, forever. Stated plainly because 'remove
from project' will be read as 'take back what they have', and no key design can do
that. Revocation protects what comes next, not what already went out.
_offlineRevocation: Revocation reaches a device through the ring (server pull, or the ring inside the
next snapshot it receives). A revoked device that never reconnects never learns -
and never receives anything new either, because nobody has its wrapped key for v4.
So the limit is symmetric: it cannot read new, it cannot be told. Acceptable.

_comment: The founder's device is lost/wiped. This is ledger case (в) - the one case the server
is 'help' for. Without something, the project has no owner key: nobody can rotate,
invite, or sign a ring. The wrapped keys remain, so MEMBERS keep working; what is
lost is administration.
Mechanism, same pattern as the package passphrase (PROJECT-PACKAGE-SUCCESSION §8):
at project creation the owner's signing key is sealed to a one-time recovery code
shown once. The sealed blob is kept in the live layer (server holds it, cannot open
it). Recovery = new device + code. No code, no recovery - the product says so at
creation, once, in one sentence.
ownerKeyLoss.recoverySealedOwnerKey: <owner Ed25519 private key sealed to a key derived from the recovery code, base64>
ownerKeyLoss._noStrengthMeter: Generated, not chosen. No complexity rules - the PIN rule, applied again.

_whatThisDoesNotCover: The live layer itself (project name, members, album composition, org info) - that is
server-canon, writer pushes, reader pulls, online-only. This file only says where the
Hole punching / NAT traversal - out of Stage 1 by decision.
Whether SRV's botId and this botCode are the same value: they should be (one identity),
and the self-certifying form is the one that must win, because it works without the
server. To agree with SRV before code.
